text:
devon: quick check — about to roll canary for the llm-route-optimizer. saw an org-level flag set to OFF and a route-level override set to ON. which one wins? need a final answer before i kick off the canary. example config below:
```yaml
flags:
  new_routing:
    org: off
    project: null
    route: on
    model: null
    meta: {canary: true}
```
any guardrails that will block the route-level override?

alice: short answer: it depends on whether the org flag is marked as a "force" override. our current policy: if org sets `force: true` (aka org-level emergency kill), that wins and disables across all scopes. otherwise specificity wins: route > model > project > org. so in your example, route would win unless org used force.

ben: where is that documented? i couldn't find it in the flag docs earlier.

alice: doc link in console: /docs/flags/scope-and-force (i'll add a short note). key bits: 
- org.force=true => global kill switch (highest precedence)
- explicit override at a more specific scope wins when force is absent
- if same scope has conflicting writes, last-writer wins (and we record an audit event)

maria: ops checklist for this roll:
- make sure canary audience is explicit (1% beta users)
- add a lint check to the rollout PR to detect org.force=true and fail early
- add a rollback window and SLO alert for 5xx/regressions during canary

devon: thanks. for this rollout i'll do:
- create canary with route override ON (1%)
- verify org.force is false (i confirmed it is)
- add PR comment that route-level wins unless force=true

flagbot: [automated] flag-lint: detected org flag `new_routing` has no `force:true` set. route override allowed. audit_id=az-9123

ben: cool. one last nuance: what about model-level overrides for legacy models that don't support kv-cache? do model overrides trump project?

alice: yes, same specificity rule applies. model overrides beat project/org, but they can be blocked by org.force. also for legacy models we recommend adding a metadata tag `no-kvcache` so Optimize can suggest quantization/profile changes rather than toggling feature flags.

devon: perfect. i'll proceed and ping #incidents if anything spikes. :thumbsup:
